items.title: Leslie Gourse interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: Of course you could recognize Lester Young versus Coleman Hawkins I guess

ctx.x: I’m very sensitive to the singers. I generally can recognize any voice, anyone singing I can recognize. I can recognize if it’s Doris Day, or Joe or of course Mel Torme, any of them. They are very distinctive. I have an easier time of recognizing them then I might say the trumpet players. I can distinguish Miles Davis in a minute. But there are some trumpet players that I don’t hear clearly. I can’t say oh that’s definitely so-and-so. Some people can, they’re very sensitive to the horn players. So I mean I hear…

So many of the veteran musicians we’ve talked to have stated how important it was back in the 30s and 40s that you establish your own sound. And that’s kind of what they were talking about. They wanted people to be able to recognize them after a few bars. Of course you could recognize Lester Young versus Coleman Hawkins I guess, but for an instrumentalist it’s a little harder than the vocalist I guess.
It depends on your ears. For me I find the vocalists much easier. There are people who as I say just immediately know who the horn player is or who the pianist is.
